clue.text: Applaud century for Eric in 27 Across

parts.note: to applaud is to clap
a ton is a hundred, a century in cricket

explanation.surface: Clapping a hundred-run innings while thinking of a guitarist in a famous band.
explanation.walkthrough: 27 Across is CREAM, the 1960s trio whose guitarist was Eric Clapton.
explanation.definitionFit: Eric Clapton was the guitarist of the rock trio Cream.

clue.text: Ancelotti notices masses in vehicles

parts.note: Carlo Ancelotti is the Italian football manager
ads are notices or advertisements

explanation.surface: A football manager notices crowds packed into cars.
explanation.definitionFit: Carloads are the quantities that fill cars, so large amounts carried in them.

clue.text: Wealth a barrier restricting disease

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: restricting means the barrier hems the disease in

parts.note: a fence is a barrier
flu is a common illness

explanation.surface: Riches act as a wall keeping illness out.
explanation.definitionFit: Affluence is abundance of money and possessions, a synonym for riches.

clue.text: Perhaps big canine finally bit Welsh runner

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word bit

parts.note: the last letter of bit is taken
the Usk is a river in Wales, and rivers run

explanation.surface: A large dog finally took a bite out of a runner from Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Canine' suggests a dog, but it is a canine tooth; 'perhaps' shows a tusk is an example of one.
explanation.definitionFit: An elephant's or walrus's tusk is an enormously enlarged tooth, often a canine.

clue.text: Wrought iron panel unmatched

indicators.note: wrought means worked or shaped, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A panel of wrought iron is beyond compare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrought iron' reads as one material, but 'wrought' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Nonpareil, from French for without equal, describes something peerless.

clue.text: Scottish bank pens unkind letters one feels

indicators.note: to pen is to enclose, so the bank's word holds the other inside it

parts.note: a brae is a Scottish hillside or bank
ill can mean unkind or hostile, as in ill will

explanation.surface: A Scottish bank's staff write nasty letters, which the recipient takes to heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' suggests money and 'letters one feels' suggests emotion; the bank is a slope and the letters are read by touch.
explanation.definitionFit: Braille is the raised-dot writing system that blind readers read with their fingertips.

clue.text: Ginger in 27 Across uses Blackberry occasionally

indicators.note: occasionally means only every other letter of the phone brand is used

parts.note: the first, third, fifth, seventh and ninth letters of the phone brand are kept

explanation.surface: A drummer in a sixties band uses a BlackBerry phone now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 27 Across is CREAM; 'Ginger' looks like a spice or hair colour, but it is the drummer's nickname.
explanation.definitionFit: Ginger Baker was the red-haired drummer of the 1960s trio Cream.

clue.text: Walks a mile with bus round behind

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: round means the bus goes around the other piece

parts.note: taken as written
behind schedule is late

explanation.surface: Someone walks a mile because the bus is late.
explanation.definitionFit: To ambulate is a formal verb meaning to move about on foot.

clue.text: Trinidadian bat devours university girl

indicators.note: devours means the batsman swallows the university letter

parts.note: Brian Lara is the great batsman from Trinidad

explanation.surface: A Caribbean cricketer gobbles up a university girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bat' could be the animal; here it is a batsman, Brian Lara of the West Indies.
explanation.definitionFit: Laura is a common female first name.

clue.text: Old diner leaving a Devon location

parts.note: ex means former

indicators.note: leaving says the letter a departs from the diner

parts.note: a diner is someone eating, an eater
taken as written

explanation.surface: A former diner walks out of a place in Devon.
explanation.walkthrough: Devon is a county in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Exeter is the county town and cathedral city of Devon.

clue.text: Trash can caught out dissenter

parts.note: refuse is rubbish or trash

indicators.note: out tells us the caught letter is to be dropped from the word before

parts.note: the can and the nick are both slang for prison
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A rubbish bin was caught out, as if in a game of cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trash can' looks like one bin, but it splits into rubbish and a slang word for jail.
explanation.definitionFit: A refusenik was a Soviet citizen refused leave to emigrate, and more widely anyone who protests by refusing.

clue.text: Jack in 27 Across the victor at Bannockburn

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Jack ..., bassist and singer of Cream
second meaning: Robert the ..., the Scottish king who won the battle in 1314

explanation.walkthrough: 27 Across is CREAM. Bannockburn was the 1314 battle where the Scots beat the English.
explanation.definitionFit: The same surname belongs to Cream's bassist and to Scotland's king Robert, winner at Bannockburn.

clue.text: Drink round, returning for work

indicators.note: returning means the drink and the round are read backwards together

parts.note: to sup is to drink
a round shape is the letter O

explanation.surface: Buying a round of drinks before going back to the office.
explanation.definitionFit: An opus is a musical or literary work, Latin for work.

clue.text: Already see changes in work-related study

indicators.note: changes says the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone notices that things have already changed at work.
explanation.walkthrough: Day release is a British scheme letting employees attend college one day a week.
explanation.definitionFit: Day release is time off from a job granted for part-time training linked to that employment.

clue.text: Brown book one dropped in old power station

parts.note: dun is a dull greyish-brown colour

indicators.note: dropped tells us the one is removed from the book

parts.note: Genesis is the first book of the Bible
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A brown book is left behind at a disused power station.
explanation.walkthrough: Dungeness, on the Kent coast, is home to a decommissioned nuclear power station.
explanation.definitionFit: Dungeness A, a Kent nuclear power station, was shut down in 2006, so it is an old plant.

clue.text: Skinny thing in Spain, dire PM ruined lives

indicators.note: ruined says the letters of these words are wrecked and reassembled

parts.note: lives means exists, which is is

explanation.surface: A weak figure in Spain, a dreadful prime minister, has wrecked people's lives.
explanation.walkthrough: E is the international vehicle code for Spain. 'Skinny' suggests thin; read it as made of skin.
explanation.definitionFit: The epidermis is the outer layer of the skin, so it is a thing of skin.

clue.text: Hat sort we use in storm

indicators.note: in storm means the letters are tossed about as if by bad weather

explanation.surface: A kind of headgear we wear in bad weather.
explanation.definitionFit: A sou'wester is a waterproof oilskin hat with a broad brim at the back.

clue.text: Short child

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a short is a small measure of spirits

explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' reads as an adjective describing the child, but it is a noun for a small drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Tot means both a small dram of liquor and a toddler.

clue.text: Player saw red — one Bronze takes on

indicators.note: takes on means the bronze colour absorbs the other pieces

parts.note: tan is a bronze colour
to see red is to rage, so saw red is raged
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An athlete fumed at only winning bronze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Player' suggests sport, but it means an actor.
explanation.definitionFit: A tragedian is an actor who specialises in tragic roles, and a player is an actor.

clue.text: Flower in day mostly not covered up?

indicators.note: mostly means the last letter of day is lost
up in a down entry means the phrase is read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: with the lid off something is uncovered

explanation.surface: A flower blooms on a day when it is mostly uncovered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not covered' must be turned into a phrase, lid off, before it is reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: The daffodil is a yellow spring flower of the narcissus family.

clue.text: Priest from the Spanish island

parts.note: el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A clergyman comes from a Spanish island.
explanation.definitionFit: Eli was the Old Testament priest who brought up Samuel.

clue.text: Novelist Alcott stopped by Scotsman in LA

indicators.note: stopped by means the Scotsman plugs a gap inside the novelist's name

parts.note: Louisa May Alcott wrote Little Women
Ian is a typical Scottish man's name

explanation.surface: The author of Little Women is halted by a Scot in Los Angeles.
explanation.walkthrough: LA looks like Los Angeles, but it is the US postal abbreviation for the state.
explanation.definitionFit: LA is the standard postal abbreviation for this southern US state.

clue.text: Winter eavesdropper?

parts.note: read as a winter eaves-dropper: something that drops from the eaves in frosty weather, not a snooping listener

explanation.walkthrough: An eavesdropper is normally a snoop; split it as eaves-dropper and it is a thing hanging from the eaves.
explanation.definitionFit: An icicle is a spike of frozen water that hangs from roof edges in cold weather.

clue.text: Supervised African land installing Evita with energy

indicators.note: installing means the African country takes the other pieces inside it

parts.note: Chad is a country in central Africa
Evita was Eva Peron, wife of the Argentine president

explanation.surface: An African country welcomes Argentina's Evita with great energy.
explanation.definitionFit: To chaperone is to accompany and oversee someone, so the past tense means watched over.

clue.text: Singer in Radiohead, electrifying

indicators.note: in signals that the answer sits inside the words that follow

parts.note: the end of the band's name runs into the start of the next word to conceal the singer

explanation.surface: A singer is thrilling as a guest with Radiohead.
explanation.definitionFit: Adele is the multi-award-winning English pop singer.

clue.text: Old boy keeping rook for Welles?

indicators.note: keeping means the old boy holds the rook within

parts.note: a son is a boy
R is the chess notation for a rook

explanation.surface: A veteran holds a chess rook in place of Welles.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark shows Welles is defined by example; Orson Welles is the one most will know.
explanation.definitionFit: Orson Welles was the director and star of Citizen Kane.

clue.text: Complacent EFSF idealists corrected

indicators.note: corrected implies the letters were wrong and must be put into a new order

explanation.surface: Idealists at the European Financial Stability Facility are put right.
explanation.walkthrough: The EFSF was the eurozone's bailout fund, which gives the surface its plausibility.
explanation.definitionFit: Being pleased with oneself to the point of smugness is what complacency means.

clue.text: Ship in vacant port over here!

indicators.note: in means the ship sits inside what remains of the port
vacant means the port is emptied of its inner letters

parts.note: only the first and last letters of port remain once it is emptied
SS is short for steamship

explanation.surface: A ship docks in an empty harbour, and someone calls out.
explanation.definitionFit: Psst is a whispered call used to attract someone's attention, like hey, over here.

clue.text: Best 1960s rock band?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the ... is the finest part, as in ... of the crop
second meaning: ..., the trio of Clapton, Bruce and Baker

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark reads 'best' as a verdict on a band; it is a separate meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means the elite or pick of something, and is also the name of the 1960s supergroup.

clue.text: See 25
US writer backed me: powerless character

indicators.note: backed tells us the word me is turned around
powerless asks us to remove the abbreviation for power from the character

parts.note: a character in a story is a person

explanation.surface: An American author has supported me, though I am a feeble figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Ralph Waldo Emerson was a nineteenth-century American essayist and poet.

clue.text: Vitamin A: recluse imports it from the East

indicators.note: from the East means read right to left, as an across answer seen from its eastern end
imports means the recluse takes the word it inside

parts.note: a recluse is a loner

explanation.surface: A hermit brings in vitamin A from Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vitamin A: ' looks like a heading, but the whole of it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Retinol is the chemical name of vitamin A, used in skincare.
